messages:
marta (Billing): heads up — major enterprise in APAC (AcroBank) rejected our invoice because they require SGD invoices tied to a local PO. They submitted PO-APAC-998 but our system issued USD. :grimacing:
Raj P: can you paste the invoice id? I can check mapping rules and FX used.
marta (Billing): invoice INV-2026-3321, customer says tax calc differs by 0.01 SGD after conversion so their AP reconcile fails (they treat rounding differently). They also tried to charge card and it was declined earlier today — might be why they expected invoice instead.
billing-bot: INV-2026-3321 status: sent, currency: USD, amount: 12,345.67 USD, linked PO: PO-APAC-998, payment_attempts: 1, last_attempt_result: card_declined (insufficient_funds).
Sofia L: quick note — local legal requires invoices in local currency for APAC entity. They asked for a VAT-bearing invoice with 7% tax line. We currently send base amounts + tax computed on USD then converted to SGD which can create tiny cent diffs.
Tom A: is this a config we can toggle per-customer? We have a per-entity prefered_currency flag but not per-invoice rounding rule.
Raj P: repro steps for eng: create invoice for customer with entity=apac_sg, prefer_currency=SGD, PO=PO-APAC-998, compute tax as local_tax_percent and then convert final totals using FX rate 1 USD = 1.35 SGD (example). Compare rounding methods: round(after-conversion) vs convert(after-rounding).
Raj P: example payload we used: 
```
POST /v1/invoices
{
  "customer_id": "acro-123",
  "entity": "global_us",
  "currency": "USD",
  "lines": [{"desc":"license","net_amount":10000}],
  "tax_percent": 7,
  "po_number": "PO-APAC-998"
}
```

marta (Billing): the customer expects: entity=apac_sg, invoice_currency=SGD, show both USD and SGD, PO pinned to local PO and VAT broken out in SGD. Their AP team rejects if the SGD VAT line is off by >0.00.
Sofia L: ask: can payments team retry card or should we issue a local-currency invoice and a credit note for the USD one? Customer prefers invoice in SGD to post to local AP.
Tom A: payments note: card decline error code is 05 (do not honor) from gateway. We flagged for retry but they asked for invoice instead. For immediate unblock, issuing local SGD invoice with same business id and linking original USD invoice via credit memo seems safest.
Raj P: engineering: two action items — (1) support generation of a local-currency invoice flow that does tax calc in local currency (compute tax on converted net or convert net+tax? customer needs convert-final then round to 2dp), and (2) expose rounding-mode per-entity (bankers vs round-away-from-zero).
Sofia L: finance ops: can you confirm whether we should use "round after conversion" for APAC customers? Customer provided example where convert-final then round to 2 decimals matched their system.
marta (Billing): finance ops OK with convert-final/round-to-2 for this customer as one-off. They also want the invoice to include PO exactly as PO-APAC-998 and show original USD amounts as reference.
billing-bot: created ticket TKT-8892 linking INV-2026-3321 -> request: generate SGD invoice + issue credit note for USD invoice. Assigned to finance-ops.
Sofia L: next steps: (1) eng to add toggle and fix conversion rounding, (2) payments to attempt second card charge if customer still prefers card, (3) billing to issue SGD invoice + credit note and resend to customer AP team.
Tom A: estimated eng effort: 2 dev days + 1 QA. Will open a PR with draft conversion utility and add `entity.rounding_mode` config.
Raj P: also log for audit: include FX rate and rounding method in invoice metadata so customer can reconcile.
marta (Billing): thanks — please keep me posted. I'll let customer know we're creating an SGD invoice and a credit note while we retry the card. :thumbsup:
